title: Orchid Labs - Budgeting, Batching & VPC Evaluation
summary: Initial discovery to map Orchid Labs' inference budget, latency targets, and security constraints. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, per-token economics, batching and KV caching, VPC/KMS requirements, and pilot scope. Agreed to share a tailored unit-econ spreadsheet and security pack; plan a short bench test with 100k tokens/day workload next week.
action_items: Ethan Morales: Send unit-econ spreadsheet and sample pricing scenarios (due 2025-12-15)
Priya Nair: Propose benchmark test plan and required telemetry (due 2025-12-16)
Rita Alvarez: Share internal SOC2/compliance checklist and KMS policy (due 2025-12-16)
Alex Chen: Provide representative prompt sets and 1-week traffic profile (due 2025-12-17)
next_steps: Redwood to send cost model + security docs
Pilot: 2-week hosted test with 100k tokens/day followed by dedicated sizing review
transcript:
00:00 Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Ethan, AE on the account. Priya and Sam are with me from SE and CSM. Can you quick intro from your side?
00:28 Alex (Orchid): Yeah hi, Alex here — CTO. Maya is our eng lead, Jordan is CFO, Rita handles security. We're trying to figure out where Redwood fits for inference: cost, latency, and whether we should go hosted, reserved (dedicated) or private VPC.
00:56 Priya (Redwood SE): Great. High level — what are your latency SLOs and typical request shapes? Helpful if you can give token distribution and sync vs async patterns.
01:22 Maya (Orchid): So for our chat assistant feature — 90% of calls are 40-120 tokens, median around 64. We also have a reranking pipeline batching a few thousand examples per hour for search. SLO aim is p95 under 300ms for the assistant.
01:48 Jordan (Orchid CFO): And budget wise we have an initial runway of $6k/mo for inference, but we can flex if the economics are clear. So per-token pricing is... like, what's typical, and where do batching and caching actually help?
02:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Okay, nice. A few quick notes: per-token pricing on Redwood hosted is usage-based; we publish tiered unit prices but we can model effective costs after batching and prefix caching. Batching helps on throughput, lowers per-token GPU time; KV cache significantly reduces repeated prefix costs for chat.
02:44 Ethan (Redwood): Also important — dedicated gives predictable throughput and a lower effective per-token when you amortize instance cost at scale, while private gives you control for compliance but adds infra overhead.
03:08 Maya (Orchid): Two quick constraints: 1) customer data can't leave our VPC for some flows, and 2) we need KMS integration for key rotation. Is private the only option there?
03:31 Rita (Orchid Security): Plus we need audit logs and RBAC integration with our SSO.
03:45 Priya (Redwood SE): You can do VPC/private for in-region custody. For hosted, we offer a VPC peering option where traffic sits over a private link and we support KMS/HSM integrations for keys — there are tradeoffs on who controls the keys. Audit logs and SAML SSO are supported across tiers but there are differences in retention and how logs are delivered for private installs.
04:16 Alex (Orchid): How bad is the latency hit if we go through VPC peering vs fully dedicated in our cloud region?
04:34 Priya (Redwood SE): Typically negligible if the private control plane is co-located; the main delta is network hop and encryption overhead — add ~10-40ms depending on region and setup. The big latency drivers are model size and batch scheduling.
04:56 Ethan (Redwood): For your 64-token median, host vs dedicated vs private has similar per-request latency once warmed. The big wins in cost are from batching for throughput-heavy jobs and caching for repeated context.
05:18 Jordan (Orchid CFO): Walk me through an example: we do 100k tokens/day at that median. What would be our monthly cost ballpark?
05:36 Priya (Redwood SE): Quick back-of-envelope: if hosted price is, say, $0.0006/token for the model family — that equals $60/day or ~$1.8k/month. But after batching (reranking + batching efficiency) and prefix KV hits (chat reuse) your effective token compute could drop 25–60% depending on cache hit rate and batch sizes. So range might be $700–$1,500/mo effective. We will send a tailored spreadsheet with scenarios.
06:12 Maya (Orchid): That $0.0006 number — is that a published rate? We saw different numbers for other vendors.
06:24 Ethan (Redwood): It's illustrative; published tiers vary by model and region. We'll include precise T&Cs and the model catalog pricing in the doc. Also, quantized/dense variants change token CPU time; we can recommend quantization options for lower-cost inference.
06:49 Alex (Orchid): You mentioned dedicated reservations reduce per-token. At our scale (100k tokens/day) does dedicated make sense?
07:04 Priya (Redwood SE): Usually dedicated is for consistent high throughput or when you need guaranteed latency and isolation — think sustained hundreds of millions tokens/day, or a business that needs reserved SLAs. At your current footprint hosted with batching is likely more cost-effective. Dedicated sizing calculators start to look better as you hit consistent multi-million tokens/month.
07:33 Jordan (Orchid CFO): Ok that's helpful. What about burst events? We have occasional spikes when marketing pushes a campaign.
07:45 Ethan (Redwood): Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies; hosted handles bursts more fluidly at the cost of less predictability. We can suggest a hybrid: start hosted, then evaluate a reserved pool after pilot data.
08:02 Maya (Orchid): Let's talk about batching & queueing — how long could requests wait to get a batched slot? We can't exceed 300ms p95 ideally.
08:16 Priya (Redwood SE): Continuous batching tries to keep latency under SLO; for 64-token median with small batches, added batching delay can be <20ms for real-time. For your reranking job we can use larger synchronous batches where latency is less critical to drive throughput.
08:39 Speaker 2 (transcript glitch): ...and then the queuing — sorry —
08:44 Maya (Orchid): (laughs) Speaker 2 is me, sorry.
08:48 Priya (Redwood SE): No worries. Back to caching — KV/prefix caching is impactful for chat where initial prompts or system messages repeat. If you have a high repeat rate KV cache hit 40-60%, you might recover a similar proportion of compute time.
09:07 Jordan (Orchid CFO): If we achieve 50% cache hits, does cost effectively halve?
09:16 Priya (Redwood SE): Not exactly halve because some tokens are in the tail and there is overhead, but you can see 35–50% reduction in compute billed for repeated prefixes. We'll model representative prompt sets to estimate your actual hit rate.
09:35 Alex (Orchid): On security, Rita — what are the must-haves?
09:40 Rita (Orchid Security): KMS, audit logs with 1-year retention, SAML SSO, RBAC and per-tenant encryption. Also we need penetration test evidence if private install.
09:55 Ethan (Redwood): We can provide SOC 2 docs and a security pack. For private installs we do supply penetration reports and deployment runbooks. For hosted, we provide a compliance bundle and we can arrange an NDA for deeper artifacts.
10:12 Alex (Orchid): Great. Another area — function/tool calling and structured outputs. We want deterministic outputs for certain flows to avoid hallucinations. Does that change cost?
10:27 Priya (Redwood SE): Model choice and prompting affect token consumption more than function-calling per se. Structured outputs can sometimes increase tokens, but we often use constrained decoding and templates which control token counts. There are tradeoffs between a heavier model for accuracy vs smaller models + prompt engineering. That influences cost.
10:50 Maya (Orchid): If we do a pilot, what telemetry do you need?
10:55 Priya (Redwood SE): We want representative prompt sets, per-request token counts, concurrency profile, and any SLA requirements. If you can give us sample traffic for a week, we can simulate batching/caching to produce a realistic unit-econ.
11:15 Alex (Orchid): We'll get that. On timeline, we want a pilot before end of Q1; decision maker is the exec team in late Jan.
11:25 Jordan (Orchid CFO): Also need to consider procurement lead time if it's a private deployment.
11:31 Ethan (Redwood): Procurement note taken. For pricing, procurement takes 2–6 weeks typically. For hosted pilot we can start much faster.
11:44 Maya (Orchid): Pricing question: is there a minimum commitment for dedicated?
11:49 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, dedicated is typically monthly reserved capacity with a minimum term depending on the offering — we'll detail that. There are also burst tiers to avoid full reserved capacity if you need flexibility.
12:02 Alex (Orchid): Competitor question — we've looked at Anthropic and a managed offering from our cloud provider. Any differentiators on cost and ops?
12:12 Ethan (Redwood): Two quick differentiators: 1) Our runtime focuses on throughput and predictable unit economics with explicit batching and cache controls; 2) deployment-mode parity — same API/rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private. Cost-wise, cloud-managed endpoints sometimes look cheaper per-call but hide inefficiencies and longer tail latencies; Anthropic has different pricing/accuracy tradeoffs. We'll include a comparison matrix.
12:38 Jordan (Orchid CFO): Okay. For the benchmark, what does Redwood need to run the test?
12:44 Priya (Redwood SE): For a hosted bench: sample prompts, expected concurrency, desired SLOs, and a contact to provision API keys. For private we need infra specs and network details. We'll draft a short runbook.
13:02 Maya (Orchid): If we choose hosted pilot, are there limits on data retention? We have to ensure logs aren't retained beyond 90 days for some datasets.
13:14 Ethan (Redwood): We have configurable retention policies and can route logs to your logging endpoint; retention and purge policies are part of enterprise settings. We'll document options.
13:29 Rita (Orchid Security): Quick on KMS — we require customer-managed keys for certain PII flows. Can Redwood support bring-your-own-key?
13:39 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes; BYOK for certain deployment types — we'll map which flows need that and the network implications.
13:52 Alex (Orchid): On model variants — how much cheaper are quantized models in practice?
13:58 Priya (Redwood SE): Quantization often reduces GPU memory pressure and can reduce inference time, giving 2x-4x improvements in throughput for some models, which translates to lower per-token cost. But quantization quality varies; we recommend evaluation on your prompts.
14:18 Jordan (Orchid CFO): So the plan sounds like: send pricing scenarios, security docs, and propose bench plan. Then run 2-week hosted pilot. After pilot we decide hosted vs dedicated vs private. Anything else?
14:31 Ethan (Redwood): That aligns. We'll add a recommended pilot budget and guardrails to the spreadsheet.
14:39 Maya (Orchid): One wrinkle — we have a legal requirement to run some inference on-prem for EU customers. Is a hybrid option supported?
14:48 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, hybrid routing is supported: route EU traffic to private nodes or on-prem connectors while keeping control plane centralized — we'll include architecture sketches.
15:00 Alex (Orchid): Ok great. Questions from our side: Jordan wants a simple monthly cost scenario at 100k tokens/day with low, mid, high cache hit rates.
15:12 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll produce low/mid/high with explicit assumptions: model, token size, batch size, cache hit rate, and expected latency.
15:28 Jordan (Orchid CFO): And we'll need SLA language to review.
15:32 Sam (Redwood CSM): We'll attach standard SLA and highlight differences per deployment mode.
15:38 Maya (Orchid): Final ops note — we use Datadog; will Redwood integrate tracing/metrics?
15:45 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we expose per-request metrics and can push to Datadog; for private we can ship logs directly.
15:53 Alex (Orchid): Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood side?
15:57 Ethan (Redwood): None — we'll prepare the package.
16:02 Maya (Orchid): Great, thanks.
16:05 Ethan (Redwood): I'll recap next steps.
16:08 Ethan (Redwood): Recap: Redwood sends unit-econ spreadsheet, security pack, bench plan; Orchid shares prompt samples and a week's traffic; schedule a 60-min bench kickoff next Wednesday; pilot to run 2 weeks.
16:27 Jordan (Orchid CFO): Agreed. If costs look favorable we'll escalate procurement.
16:33 Rita (Orchid Security): I'll review the security pack and get back with any blockers.
16:38 Ethan (Redwood): Thanks everyone — we'll send the materials by Monday.
16:42 Alex (Orchid): Thanks all, bye.
16:45 End of recording.
